School.title: School
School.description: Represents a school where professors teach and students learn.

id.description: Unique identifier for the School entity.

name.description: The official name of the school.

address.description: The street address of the school.

city.description: The city where the school is located.

state.description: The state or province where the school is located.

zipCode.description: The postal code of the school's location.

phoneNumber.description: The contact phone number for the school.

email.description: The official email address for the school.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the school record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the school record was last updated.

ProfessorProfile.title: ProfessorProfile
ProfessorProfile.description: Stores profile information for a professor, linked to an external authentication system user ID.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ProfessorProfile entity, typically matching an external user ID.

firstName.description: The first name of the professor.

lastName.description: The last name of the professor.

email.description: The contact email address of the professor.

schoolId.description: Reference to the School the professor is affiliated with. (Relationship: School 1:N ProfessorProfile)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the professor profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the professor profile was last updated.

Subject.title: Subject
Subject.description: Defines academic subjects or disciplines, such as Mathematics or Portuguese.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subject entity.

description.description: A brief description of the subject.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the subject record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the subject record was last updated.

Classroom.title: Classroom
Classroom.description: Represents a specific class group for students in a particular academic year and taught by a professor.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Classroom entity.

name.description: The name of the classroom (e.g., '3º Ano A - Vespertino').

academicYear.description: The academic year this classroom pertains to (e.g., 2023).

professorId.description: Reference to the ProfessorProfile who teaches this classroom. (Relationship: ProfessorProfile 1:N Classroom)

subjectIds.description: References to Subjects taught in this classroom. (Relationship: Classroom N:N Subject)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the classroom record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the classroom record was last updated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Student entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the student.

lastName.description: The last name of the student.

classroomIds.description: References to Classrooms the student is enrolled in. (Relationship: Student N:N Classroom)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the student record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the student record was last updated.

Exam.title: Exam
Exam.description: Represents a specific test, quiz, or assessment administered to students.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Exam entity.

title.description: The title of the exam (e.g., 'Avaliação de Geometria - 1º Bimestre').

description.description: A brief description of the exam.

classroomId.description: Reference to the Classroom where this exam was administered. (Relationship: Classroom 1:N Exam)

subjectId.description: Reference to the Subject this exam covers. (Relationship: Subject 1:N Exam)

professorId.description: Reference to the ProfessorProfile who created or administered this exam. (Relationship: ProfessorProfile 1:N Exam)

dateAdministered.description: The date and time when the exam was administered.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the exam record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the exam record was last updated.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Defines an individual question within an exam, including its correct answer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Question entity.

examId.description: Reference to the Exam this question belongs to. (Relationship: Exam 1:N Question)

questionNumber.description: The sequential number or order of the question within its exam.

text.description: The full text of the question, if applicable.

correctAnswer.description: The official correct answer for this question.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the question record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the question record was last updated.

StudentExamAttempt.title: StudentExamAttempt
StudentExamAttempt.description: Records a student's overall attempt and performance on a specific exam.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StudentExamAttempt entity.

studentId.description: Reference to the Student who made this attempt. (Relationship: Student 1:N StudentExamAttempt)

examId.description: Reference to the Exam this attempt is for. (Relationship: Exam 1:N StudentExamAttempt)

score.description: The total score obtained by the student for this exam attempt.

percentage.description: The percentage score achieved by the student (score / total possible score).

dateAttempted.description: The date and time when the student attempted the exam.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the student exam attempt record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the student exam attempt record was last updated.

StudentAnswer.title: StudentAnswer
StudentAnswer.description: Records an individual student's response to a specific question within an exam attempt.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StudentAnswer entity.

studentExamAttemptId.description: Reference to the StudentExamAttempt this answer belongs to. (Relationship: StudentExamAttempt 1:N StudentAnswer)

questionId.description: Reference to the Question this answer is for. (Relationship: Question 1:N StudentAnswer)

studentResponse.description: The answer provided by the student for this question.

isCorrect.description: Indicates whether the student's response was correct.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the student answer record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the student answer record was last updated.

Certificate.title: Certificate
Certificate.description: Represents a generated certificate for a student.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Certificate entity.

studentName.description: The name of the student receiving the certificate.

activityName.description: The name of the activity or achievement.

date.description: The date mentioned in the certificate.

verificationCode.description: A unique random code for verification.

professorId.description: Reference to the professor who generated the certificate.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the certificate was created.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling, with a strong emphasis on Data Clarity and Predictability. All professor-specific data is organized under a top-level `/users/{professorId}` collection, leveraging path-based ownership. This ensures that a professor's data (profile, classrooms, students, exams, attempts, and answers) is inherently secured by checking `request.auth.uid` against the `{professorId}` wildcard in the path.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization (Strategy A):**
Crucially, to eliminate `get()` calls in security rules and enable atomic operations, authorization-relevant parent attributes are denormalized into child documents:

*   **Classroom, Student, Exam, Question:** Documents in these subcollections will explicitly include `professorId` (matching the path parameter) and `schoolId` (from the professor's profile). This allows security rules to evaluate ownership and affiliation directly from the document's data without needing to retrieve parent documents.
*   **StudentExamAttempt:** This document is critical for student performance tracking. It will denormalize `professorId`, `studentId` (from its path), but also `schoolId`, `classroomId`, `examId`, and `subjectId` (from the linked Exam and ProfessorProfile). This comprehensive denormalization supports complex queries and ensures that a rule can confirm a professor's access to an attempt by checking its fields directly.
*   **StudentAnswer:** Similarly, `StudentAnswer` documents will denormalize `professorId`, `studentId`, `studentExamAttemptId` (from its path), and also `schoolId`, `classroomId`, `examId`, `subjectId`, and `questionId` (from the linked ExamAttempt/Exam/Question). This level of detail makes each `StudentAnswer` document self-contained for authorization purposes.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structural segregation and denormalization strategy directly support efficient and secure `list` operations (Query-Able Paths):

*   **Professor-owned data:** For collections like `/users/{professorId}/classrooms`, `/users/{professorId}/students`, `/users/{professorId}/classrooms/{classroomId}/exams`, etc., listing operations inherently retrieve only data owned by the authenticated professor because `request.auth.uid` is part of the path. Security rules will simply confirm `request.auth.uid == professorId` on read access, ensuring that no server-side filtering is required for basic ownership-based lists.
*   **Cross-context queries:** For more complex queries, such as listing all `StudentExamAttempts` for a specific `classroomId` or `schoolId` (within a professor's domain), the denormalized `classroomId` and `schoolId` fields in the `StudentExamAttempt` documents enable efficient `.where()` queries. The security rules will then verify that `request.auth.uid` matches the `professorId` denormalized in the document itself, preventing unauthorized access while supporting flexible data retrieval without filtering.

**Structural Segregation (Strategy B):**
Global entities like `School` and `Subject` are in their own top-level collections (`/schools`, `/subjects`), indicating a broader accessibility. Professor-specific data is strictly nested under `/users/{professorId}`, clearly separating data with different security postures.

This design minimizes rule complexity, enhances debuggability, and ensures scalability by avoiding expensive `get()` calls in rules and supporting efficient client-side queries.
